summary: An informational memo from Ipsilon Networks specifying version 2.0 of the General Switch Management Protocol, which lets a controller manage an ATM switch. It extends the earlier version of GSMP and was written as a vendor description, not a standard.

eli5.summary: A switch is like a train yard junction. This memo describes the messages a controller uses to tell the junction which tracks to connect.

questions: how does the gsmp adjacency protocol work
subtitle: How a controller tells an ATM switch to set up connections, report status and offer quality of service.

tldr.problem: An ATM switch needs an outside controller to establish and release connections, manage ports and read configuration and statistics.
tldr.mechanism: GSMP is a master-slave protocol: the controller sends request messages and the switch replies, and an adjacency protocol first synchronizes state and agrees on a version. Version 2 adds Quality of Service messages.
tldr.outcome: It is an Informational vendor memo that updates RFC 1987, and it says it does not specify an Internet standard of any kind.

today: RFC 2297 is Informational and updates RFC 1987. It has not been obsoleted or updated, but it is a vendor description that says it specifies no Internet standard.

sections.title: What GSMP Controls
sections.content:
The General Switch Management Protocol (GSMP) is a general purpose protocol to control an ATM switch. A controller can establish and release connections across the switch, add and delete leaves on a multicast connection, manage ports, and request configuration and statistics. The switch can also report asynchronous events such as a link going down.

GSMP is asymmetric: the controller is the master and the switch the slave. It runs over a control virtual channel on an ATM link, or over Ethernet, and one controller can manage several switches using separate control connections. A virtual channel connection joins an incoming virtual channel to one or more outgoing ones, identified by input port and VPI/VCI. GSMP supports point-to-point and point-to-multipoint connections.

This version is an enhancement of GSMP version 1.1 (RFC 1987). The main addition is Quality of Service (QoS) messages, along with improvements from operational experience.
sections.eli5: The controller is the boss who tells the switch which incoming wire to join to which outgoing wire. The switch does what it is told and reports back.

sections.title: Encapsulation and Message Header
sections.content:
Over ATM, GSMP packets are carried directly in an AAL-5 CPCS-PDU with an LLC/SNAP header; the Ethertype assigned to GSMP is 0x880C. The default control channel is VPI 0, VCI 15. The MTU of the GSMP message field is 1492 octets. Over Ethernet, messages carry source and destination MAC addresses and, for non-adjacency messages, the Sender Instance and Receiver Instance fields as extra protection against corrupt state. Receivers must discard messages whose addresses or instance numbers do not match what the adjacency protocol stored.

Every message except the adjacency message starts with Version, Message Type, Result, Code and a Transaction Identifier that ties a response to its request. In a request, Result is NoSuccessAck (1) or AckAll (2). In a response it is Success (3), Failure (4) or More (5), where More means further messages complete the response. Unused or reserved fields must be zero when sent and ignored when received.
sections.eli5: Every message starts with the same labelled front page: which version of the rules, what kind of message, and a ticket number so the answer can be matched to the question.

sections.title: Message Classes and Failures
sections.content:
There are five classes of request-response message: Connection Management, Port Management, State and Statistics, Configuration, and Quality of Service. The switch may also send Event messages (Port Up, Port Down, Invalid VPI/VCI, New Port, Dead Port), which the controller does not acknowledge. Connection management covers Add Branch, Delete Tree, Verify Tree, Delete All, Delete Branches and Move Branch.

Switch ports have a 32-bit port number assigned by the switch, and a port session number that changes when a port comes back up. A request with the wrong session number must be rejected, which lets the controller detect link failure and keep state in step. A failure response is the request message returned with Result 4 and a failure code, for example 3 for a request not implemented, 8 for a connection that does not exist, or 15 for out of resources. No change should be made to switch state when a failure is returned.

Section 12 marks a minimal set as Required, including Add Branch VCC (16), Delete Branches (17), Port Management (32), Port Statistics (49), the three Configuration messages (64 to 66) and the adjacency protocol (10).
sections.eli5: The boss can ask the switch to connect wires, check ports, or send counts. If the switch cannot do something, it hands the note back with a number saying why.

sections.title: Quality of Service
sections.content:
Version 2 adds a rich set of QoS messages: QoS Configuration, Scheduler Establishment, QoS Class Establishment, QoS Release and QoS Connection Management. They are optional. Without them, each connection can simply be given a priority when established, and a higher priority cell is much more likely to leave the switch first.

The messages rest on an abstract switch model of four functions. A policer can discard or tag cells to enforce an upper bound. A classifier groups connections into a QoS class that shares resources, while cell order within each connection must be preserved. A regulator either polices (tag, discard or differentiated scheduling of conforming and excess cells) or shapes by pacing cells at a set rate. A scheduler then serves traffic onto the output port.
sections.eli5: QoS is like lanes at a toll booth. Some cars get a fast lane and others wait in the normal one, and the controller decides who goes where.

sections.title: The Adjacency Protocol
sections.content:
GSMP is a hard state protocol, so the adjacency protocol synchronizes state across the link, agrees on a version, learns who is at the other end and detects when that changes. Apart from adjacency messages, nothing may be sent until synchronization is reached, and other messages received before then are discarded.

Its message has Message Type 10 and four codes: SYN (1), SYNACK (2), ACK (3) and RSTACK (4). An M flag shows whether the sender is master or slave, so a master never synchronizes with another master. In a SYN the version is the highest the sender understands, and a receiver replies with a lower version it understands. This specification is Version 2. The Timer field is in units of 100ms, with one second suggested as the period. The state machine moves SYNSENT, SYNRCVD and ESTAB, and ESTAB means synchronized.

If no valid GSMP messages arrive for more than three times the announced timer value, loss of synchronization may be declared. A switch may then try a backup controller without resetting state, or simply reset and search for a controller.
sections.eli5: Before talking, the two sides shake hands: each says who it is and which rules it knows. If one goes quiet for too long, they start over.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The memo assumes physical security on the control link between controller and switch. It states that security issues are not discussed in the document. The only protection against corrupt state it describes is the use of instance numbers and port session numbers.
sections.eli5: The memo assumes nobody can sneak a wire between the boss and the switch, so it does not say how to lock the connection.

fields.name: Version
fields.desc: GSMP version negotiated by the adjacency protocol.

fields.name: Result
fields.desc: Whether an acknowledgement is wanted, or the outcome of a request.

fields.name: Code
fields.desc: Further detail, mostly the failure code.

fields.name: Transaction Identifier
fields.desc: Associates a request with its response.

items.label: SYN
items.desc: Starts synchronization and carries the highest version understood.

items.label: SYNACK
items.desc: Answers a SYN, using the agreed version.
